help.title: How “What changed” works
help.intro: Six automatic checks run over your team's data and flag anything outside its usual range, so you don't have to sweep every dashboard tab looking for it.
help.window_body: The last completed week against a fixed 8-week trailing baseline. This window is deliberately independent of the date filter above — “normal” is a property of your team, not of the range you happen to have selected, so switching to All time won't change what counts as unusual. The team and Products filters do apply.
help.severity_high: Red — well outside the normal range; worth looking at today.
help.severity_medium: Amber — outside the normal range; worth a glance.
help.severity_low: Grey — a shift worth knowing about, not necessarily a problem.
help.quiet_body: Every check needs a meaningful volume of work before it fires, not just a big ratio — a tripling of two hours isn't a finding. At most six are shown, highest severity first, and the rest are counted at the bottom. With under four weeks of history the baseline comparisons switch off and the panel says so.

account_burn_spike.name: Account or opportunity burn spike
account_burn_spike.body: One record consumed far more hours than it usually does. Measured against that record's own average, over the weeks it was actually worked — SE engagement is lumpy, so a quiet stretch shouldn't make the next burst look alarming.

contributor_over_capacity.name: Contributor over capacity
contributor_over_capacity.body: Someone logged well above their capacity target for the week, adjusted for PTO and holidays. Runs even for a brand-new team, since it needs no history.

contributor_logging_stopped.name: Contributor stopped logging
contributor_logging_stopped.body: Someone with an established logging habit recorded nothing this week. Only fires for people who were consistent before — sporadic loggers aren't flagged as having stopped.

activity_type_shift.name: Activity type surge or collapse
activity_type_shift.body: One activity type moved sharply against its own 8-week average — for example Demo hours halving, or {{evalWork}} tripling. Often the earliest sign of a change in where the team's effort is going.

unlinked_spike.name: Unlinked activity spike
unlinked_spike.body: An unusual share of submitted activities have no {{crm}} link at all. That work is invisible to everyone outside ImpactIQ, and a jump usually means either a broken habit or a broken {{crm}} connection.

crm_provider.none_body: No CRM: activities aren't linked to a CRM or written back to one. Choose a CRM here at any time.
crm_provider.inactive_note_other: {{active}} is the CRM right now. You can set up {{name}} here first; ImpactIQ only uses it once {{name}} is chosen as the CRM above.

crm_features.title: CRM features
crm_features.description: App-wide switches for optional CRM features. They apply to every team and to whichever CRM this install uses.
crm_features.campaigns_hint: Linking activities to Campaigns, the Campaign search tab, and Campaign views and counts on dashboards. When off, nothing is deleted: activities already linked to a Campaign keep that link.
crm_features.campaigns_unavailable_hubspot: The connected HubSpot portal has no Campaigns (they need Marketing Hub and the marketing.campaigns.read scope), so they stay hidden. Run Check access on the HubSpot card after adding them.
crm_features.leads_hint: Linking activities to Leads, the Lead search tab, Lead views and counts on dashboards, and converted Leads in the Account rollup. When off, nothing is deleted: activities already linked to a Lead keep that link.
crm_features.leads_unavailable_hubspot: The connected HubSpot portal has no Leads (they need the crm.objects.leads.read scope on a tier that includes them), so they stay hidden. Run Check access on the HubSpot card after adding them.
crm_features.campaigns_off_confirm: Turn off Campaigns for everyone? Campaign search, Campaign links and Campaign dashboard views will be hidden. Existing Campaign links are kept and come back if you turn this on again.
crm_features.leads_off_confirm: Turn off Leads for everyone? Lead search, Lead links and Lead dashboard views will be hidden. Existing Lead links are kept and come back if you turn this on again.
crm_features.hubspot_meetings_hint: Before creating a meeting in HubSpot, ImpactIQ looks for the same meeting already logged by HubSpot's own calendar sync (same owner, start and end time) and fills that one in instead: activity type, notes as internal notes, and Deal and Company links. Turn this off if your reps sync their calendars to HubSpot: ImpactIQ then never creates a meeting, and an activity with no match yet checks again later. Tasks are always created.
crm_features.hubspot_meetings_off_confirm: Stop ImpactIQ creating meetings in HubSpot? Approved meetings will only be linked to a meeting HubSpot's calendar sync already logged; until one appears, the activity shows a CRM Sync issue and is checked again on the retry schedule.

evaluation_source.not_available_yet: Not available in this version yet
evaluation_source.locked_reason: Locked: activities already link to Projects from {{source}}
evaluation_source.change_confirm: Change the Project source from {{from}} to {{to}}?
evaluation_source.off_confirm: Turn Projects off? The Project picker, chips, Engineer Notes posting and the Project dashboards will be hidden for everyone, and CriteriaIQ stops as a secondary source. Saved Project links are kept.
evaluation_source.locked_body: {{formatted}} activities link to Projects from {{source}}, so the primary source can only move between {{source}} and Off.
evaluation_source.unlocked_body: No activity links to a Project yet, so the primary source can still be changed freely.
evaluation_source.off_body: Projects are off. The Project picker, Project chips and panels, posting to Engineer Notes, and the Won w/o {{evalTerm}} and Project-Specific Costing dashboards are hidden for everyone. Saved Project links are kept and come back when Projects are turned on again.
evaluation_source.secondary_label: Use CriteriaIQ as a secondary source
evaluation_source.secondary_hint: With the CRM object as primary, CriteriaIQ adds criteria progress and a link to the CriteriaIQ project. The CRM keeps its values. Never locked.
evaluation_source.secondary_on_confirm: Use CriteriaIQ as a secondary Project source?
evaluation_source.secondary_off_confirm: Stop using CriteriaIQ as a secondary Project source?
evaluation_source.criteriaiq_primary_body: CriteriaIQ is the Project source. criteriaiq.title: CriteriaIQ connection
criteriaiq.description: ImpactIQ reads CriteriaIQ projects with a CriteriaIQ API key. It never writes to CriteriaIQ.
criteriaiq.test_ok: CriteriaIQ answered and the key can read projects.
criteriaiq.key_on_file: Key on file ending {{hint}} (leave blank to keep it)
criteriaiq.key_hint: Create the key in CriteriaIQ under Admin › Integrations › n8n › API Keys, with Access set to Read only. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
criteriaiq.private_network_label: CriteriaIQ runs on our private network (allows a private address, and plain http:// only for a private address). Loopback and cloud metadata addresses stay blocked.
criteriaiq.remove_confirm: Remove the CriteriaIQ connection? The stored API key is deleted.
criteriaiq.lookup_title: Find CriteriaIQ projects for an Evaluation
criteriaiq.lookup_hint: Enter a Salesforce Evaluation record id to see which CriteriaIQ projects point at it. This is the lookup ImpactIQ uses to pair a Project with its CriteriaIQ project.
criteriaiq.lookup_none: No CriteriaIQ project points at that record.

live_refresh.title: Live refresh
live_refresh.description: CriteriaIQ tells ImpactIQ when a project changes, so CriteriaIQ details refresh within seconds instead of after a few minutes, and, with CriteriaIQ as the Project source, the linked activities' Project details update right away instead of overnight.
live_refresh.rotate_confirm: Make a new signing secret? The current one stops working at once, so update the webhook in CriteriaIQ straight after.
live_refresh.turn_off_confirm: Turn off live refresh? CriteriaIQ details go back to refreshing every few minutes and overnight.
live_refresh.secret_once: Copy the secret now. It is stored encrypted and not shown again.
live_refresh.secret_on_file: Signing secret on file ending {{hint}}. Click New secret if you need it again.
live_refresh.setup: In CriteriaIQ, open Admin › Integrations › Webhooks and add a Generic HTTP webhook with this URL. Paste the secret into Signing Secret under Advanced Settings, and tick project.created, project.updated, project.status_changed, criteria.updated, criteria.completed and the MAP status_changed events.
live_refresh.never_received: No update received from CriteriaIQ yet.

hubspot.remove_confirm: Remove the HubSpot connection? The stored token and the copied owner list are deleted.
hubspot.check_none: Not checked yet. Click Check access to see what this token can do.
hubspot.status_missing: Missing: add this scope to the private app, or the portal's plan lacks it

gong.workspaces_none: This Gong tenant has no workspaces.

codes.duplicate_app_field: “{{appField}}” is mapped {{count}} times. Only the first mapping is used ({{winner}}); the rest are ignored.
codes.duplicate_sf_field: Several app fields ({{appFields}}) write to the same {{crm}} field. The last one wins.
codes.missing_required_app_field: No active mapping for “{{appField}}”. The sync will still run, but this value never reaches {{crm}}.
codes.read_only_on_required: “{{appField}}” is mapped read-only, so it's never written to {{crm}}.
codes.refresh_only_on_required: “{{appField}}” is marked refresh-only, so it's pulled from {{crm}} but never written back.
codes.unknown_app_field: “{{appField}}” isn't an app field the sync reads, so this mapping has no effect.
codes.no_mappings: This object has {{types}} active activity type(s) but no active mappings — every sync would create an empty record.
codes.no_activity_types: No active activity type writes to this object.
codes.dry_run_unavailable: This isn't an activity write-back object, so a dry-run payload preview isn't available here. The static and field-level checks above still apply.
codes.describe_failed: Couldn't read this object's fields from {{crm}}, so field-level checks were skipped.
codes.field_not_found: “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” doesn't exist on this object in your {{crm}} org.
codes.not_createable: “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” can't be written to (it's a {{type}} field). {{crm}} will reject the record.
codes.not_updateable: “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” can be set on create but not updated, so re-syncing an existing record will fail.
codes.type_mismatch: “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” is a {{{{crmType}} field, but this mapping sends a {{expected}} value.
codes.constant_too_long: The constant on “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” is {{actual}} characters; the field holds {{length}}.
codes.constant_not_in_picklist: “{{value}}” isn't an allowed picklist value for “{{{{crmFieldApi}}”.
codes.type_not_in_picklist: Activity type “{{type}}” resolves to “{{value}}”, which isn't in the “{{{{crmFieldApi}}” picklist.

backup.intro_included: A backup is a complete copy of the application database: every team, user, activity, setting, theme (including logos and the login screen graphic), integration configuration and history. Use it to keep a safe copy, or to move ImpactIQ to a new install.
backup.intro_excluded: Environment variables and server secrets (DATABASE_URL, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, SESSION_SECRET, APP_URL and the rest) are not included; each install keeps its own. Sign-in sessions are not included either, and this install keeps its own public URL setting.
backup.intro_key: Saved Salesforce and Outlook connections, MFA secrets and integration secrets are stored encrypted with TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. They only work after a restore if the new install uses the same key; otherwise users reconnect and admins re-enter integration secrets.
backup.intro_sensitive: The backup file contains password hashes and encrypted credentials. Store it somewhere only administrators can reach.
backup.export_body: Downloads the whole database as one compressed file. The app keeps working while the export runs, and the file reflects a single consistent moment.
backup.import_body: Upload a backup file to see exactly what it contains before anything changes. Restoring replaces ALL data in this install with the backup's data, in a single step that is rolled back completely if anything fails.

setup.subtitle: Configure your deployment in a few quick steps

step1.title: Database Connection
step1.description: Enter your Postgres connection string. We'll test the connection and run migrations automatically.

step3.title: Security Keys
step3.description: These 256-bit keys sign session cookies and encrypt Salesforce OAuth tokens at rest. Generate new ones or paste your own.
step3.warning: Once set, do not change this key — doing so invalidates all stored Salesforce tokens.
step3.invalid: Must be a 64-character hexadecimal string (32 bytes).
step3.session_key_hint: Signs session cookies. Safe to regenerate anytime — doing so just signs everyone out.

step4.title: Application URL
step4.description: The public URL where users access ImpactIQ. Used for OAuth callbacks and email links.
step4.hint: Include the protocol (https://) and no trailing slash.

step5.title: Okta SSO (Optional)
step5.description: Connect Okta for single sign-on. Users will get a "Sign in with Okta" button on the login page.
step5.optional_note: Optional — you can configure this later by editing your .env file.
step5.setup_hint: In Okta: create an OIDC web app, add the redirect URI above, copy the Client ID and Secret here.

step6.description: Connect a Salesforce Connected App to enable per-user OAuth and activity write-back to SF Events/Tasks.
step6.login_url_hint: Use https://test.salesforce.com for sandboxes. Default: https://login.salesforce.com
step6.optional_note: Optional — you can configure this later by editing your .env file.

step7.optional_note: Optional — you can configure this later by editing your .env file.
step7.setup_hint: In Azure: register an app, add Calendars.Read and User.Read API permissions, create a client secret.

step8.title: AI Assistant (Optional)
step8.description: Connect an AI provider for activity type suggestions and the notes features. Without one, ImpactIQ uses keyword rules only.
step8.optional_note: Optional: you can add or change providers later on Admin → Integrations → AI Assistant.

how_to_use.title: How to Use ImpactIQ
how_to_use.subtitle: A complete walkthrough of the app for every role. Start here if you're new.
how_to_use.overview_body:
ImpactIQ is a revenue-capacity intelligence platform that connects technical and channel activity to {{crm}}, creating a common view of resource consumption, opportunity coverage, utilization, and future capacity requirements.

**The core problem:** Team capacity is invisible. Leaders make resourcing decisions without knowing where time is actually going. Contributors have no easy way to log work that doesn't fit neatly into a CRM task.

**The solution:** A contributor-first activity logging tool anchored to the Outlook calendar, with {{crm}} as the system of record for deal context, leadership dashboards derived from what contributors actually log, and a multi-team architecture so different teams (SE, Channel, Sales) each have their own activity types, rulesets, and {{crmShort}} configuration.

Its business case should answer five leadership questions:

1. Where are SE and Channel resources spending their time?
2. Which opportunities, accounts, campaigns, and partners are consuming capacity?
3. Are the right opportunities receiving the right level of technical support?
4. Where will capacity constraints affect future revenue?
5. When should the organization rebalance resources, hire, or change coverage models?

**ImpactIQ is a capacity planning tool, not a performance review tool.** It exists to answer those questions directly, not to rank or score individuals. You'll see this same note on the activity logging screen itself.

There are four roles:

- **Contributor** (SE, Channel, Sales rep): logs their own activities, sees the team's finalized (submitted) activity, and never sees other people's drafts.
- **Team Leader**: read-only dashboards for capacity, activity mix, and coverage on the team(s) they lead. Cannot edit anyone's activity.
- **Team Admin**: everything a Leader can see, plus configuration for their own team: activity types, keyword/nudge rules, capacity groups, user roles.
- **App Admin**: full access across every team: integrations, themes, role permissions, audit log, and every monitoring page.

A single person can hold different roles on different teams (for example, Team Admin on Sales Engineering and plain Contributor on Channel).
how_to_use.contributor_body:
Your home screen is the **Weekly View**: an activity list on the left, grouped by day, with the Outlook calendar for that week in a collapsible panel on the right. Click any calendar event and it pre-fills a new activity's title, times, and effort hours.

#### Two ways to log
- **From the calendar**: click an event in the right-hand panel; the form opens pre-filled. This is the fastest path and the one to use for any real meeting.
- **Manually**: click **+ Log Activity** for work with no calendar event (write-ups, prep time, ad-hoc support).

#### Draft vs. Submitted
Every activity starts as a **draft** and stays private to you until you **Submit** it. Only submitted activities count toward your team's leader dashboards and {{crm}} write-back; drafts are yours alone. You can freely edit any activity for **90 days** after it was created; after that it becomes read-only for you (an App Admin can still edit it any time).

#### The suggestion engine
When you open a calendar event to log it, ImpactIQ tries to suggest an Activity Type automatically, in this order: (1) your team's admin-configured **keyword rules**, (2) your own personal **Non-Activity keywords** (My Settings), (3) **Azure OpenAI** as a fallback. A suggestion is always just a suggestion: you confirm or change it before saving, and it never auto-selects without you.

#### Non-Activity
Not every calendar event is work you want to log: 1:1s, internal syncs, personal blocks. Click **Non-Activity** on a suggested meeting card (or let a keyword rule / your own Non-Activity keyword list do it automatically) to make it disappear from your day list. This never creates or deletes a real activity record; it's fully reversible from the calendar event's details.

#### Subtypes
Some teams break an Activity Type down into more specific **Subtypes** (for example, Discovery → Technical Discovery / Architecture Discovery). If your team has Subtypes turned on and the Activity Type you picked has any defined, choosing one is required before you can save. The per-Activity-Type **Guide** page (the page you opened this from) lists every type's available Subtypes right alongside its "when to use this" guidance, so it's the place to check both together.

#### Remote vs. On-site & travel costs
Every activity is **Remote** by default. Switching it to **On-site** opens an Incidental Costs panel where you can record real travel spend (Transportation, Lodging, and Food while travelling) in your own display currency. This isn't required to save the activity, but if the on-site work genuinely cost you travel money, entering it here is how that gets captured; switching back to Remote clears and deletes any costs you'd entered (you'll be asked to confirm first). These figures aren't folded into the app's cost dashboards yet (a banner on Most Expensive and the User Leaderboard says so), so think of this as capturing the record accurately now, ahead of that landing.

#### Templates & bulk import
Save any activity as a **Template** for one-click re-use on recurring work, and use **Approve with template** to accept a suggested meeting pre-filled from a saved template in one click. If you have a backlog of past work to catch up on, use the **CSV import** (My Settings → Data & Templates) instead of logging one at a time.

#### If a logged meeting disappears from Outlook
If you approve an activity from a calendar meeting and that meeting is later deleted in Outlook, ImpactIQ doesn't lose track of it; it flags the activity for a decision instead of leaving it pointing at nothing. A **"This Week's Deleted Activities"** section appears above your day list (and a header banner links straight to it) so you can either **Keep** it as a standalone ImpactIQ/{{crm}} record with a "Not In Outlook" badge, or **Delete** it everywhere, the only permanent delete in the app, including the {{crm}} copy. This is only ever flagged after ImpactIQ successfully re-checks your calendar, so a temporary network hiccup is never mistaken for a real deletion.
how_to_use.salesforce_body:
Every activity can (and usually should) link to a {{crm}} record so the hours show up against the right deal.

#### Four ways to link
The {{crm}} Link search has four tabs: **Opportunity**, **Account**, **Lead**, and **Campaign**. Which tab you search from decides exactly what the activity links to; ImpactIQ never guesses. By default, Opportunity search is filtered to deals where you're the Assigned SE, Primary Engineer, Specialist Engineer, or a Supporting Engineer; click **Open Search** to search beyond that filter. Campaigns roll up to an Account through their linked Opportunity; Leads roll up to an Account only after they're converted; an unconverted Lead stands on its own.

#### Record preview
Hover (or keyboard-focus) an Opportunity or Account name on an activity card to see its current {{crm}} state (stage, forecast, amount, close date, owner) without leaving the page.

#### Support Tickets
If your team has it turned on, the activity form lets you attach one or more {{crm}} support tickets, searched by default against the linked Account. This is a read-only link-out; it never writes anything to {{crm}}.

#### Notes → {{crm}}
A note you write on an activity can be pushed to {{crm}} as a `ContentNote` on the linked Opportunity or Account, and, for a linked Project/Evaluation record, appended as a dated update to Engineer Notes without erasing what's already there. All {{crm}} writes happen asynchronously in the background; you'll never be blocked waiting on a sync, and a failed sync shows a retry option.

#### When a {{crm}} link breaks
Two different things can go wrong after you've linked an activity, and ImpactIQ tells them apart rather than showing one generic error:
- **The linked record itself was deleted in {{crm}}**: the Opportunity, Account, Lead, or linked Project you originally picked. ImpactIQ detects this automatically (a nightly check, plus a live check whenever you open that activity) and shows an **"{{crmShort}} link broken"** badge on the card. Nothing is locked; it's simply a signal to re-link the activity if it should point somewhere else now.
- **The {{crm}} Event or Task ImpactIQ itself created was deleted directly in {{crm}}**: the meeting/task record the sync wrote, not the Opportunity or Account it points to. ImpactIQ can't flag this on its own the way it flags the case above: the next time that activity tries to sync (for example, after you edit it), the write fails and shows up as a Sync Issue your Team or App Admin can see on Admin → CRM Sync. If a sync keeps failing for no reason you can explain, that's the place to ask your admin to check.
how_to_use.nudges_body:
A **nudge** is a friendly reminder your Team Admin configured, for example, "nothing logged this week yet" or "no {{evalWork}} logged for this Opportunity in 14 days." Nudges show up in three places that all stay in sync: the notification **bell**, a banner on your Weekly View, and a toast at the bottom of the screen.

There are three actions:
- **Mark read** (checkmark): clears it for today; it can come back tomorrow if the underlying condition is still true.
- **Snooze** (bell icon): pick 1, 7, or 30 days to silence it.
- **Close out** (X, bell only): permanently stops that specific nudge. This option is deliberately only on the notification bell, not the quick-glance card or toast, so a reminder can't be silenced forever by a stray click.
how_to_use.leader_body:
If you're a Team Leader, Team Admin, or App Admin, the **Dashboard** page gives you read-only reporting across your team(s), always built from **submitted** activity only, never drafts. Dashboards are organized into 10 groups:

- **Capacity**: team heatmap, this-week utilization, capacity trend over time
- **Activity**: activity-type breakdown, activity mix, plan vs. actual, subtype breakdown
- **Accounts**: Account/Opportunity burn and concentration, most-expensive records
- **Health**: logging compliance, logging lag, week-over-week delta
- **Products**: effort hours by product
- **Revenue**: Opportunity ROI (ACV vs. hours), cost per $ of ACV
- **Manager**: cross-team rollups, the user leaderboard, and single-team deep-dives
- **Infrastructure**: cost/hours/ACV grouped by Project (Evaluation)
- **Coverage**: Attach Rate, how much of a rep's pipeline actually has SE engagement
- **History**: read-only pre-ImpactIQ {{crm}} activity, with estimated hours only

Most dashboards share a filter row (date range, Subteam, Team member, Products, and on the Manager/Revenue/Accounts groups, Sales Stage and Forecast Category) plus a **Refresh from {{crm}}** button.

#### "What changed" panel
Every dashboard tab has a collapsible **What changed** panel above the content: a short, automatic list of anything unusual in the last completed week compared to a rolling 8-week baseline: a burn spike on an account, a contributor who stopped logging, an activity-type surge, or {{crm}} sync failures. It deliberately stays quiet (capped at 6 findings, and off entirely when there isn't enough history to judge) so it doesn't become wallpaper.
how_to_use.scheduling_body:
The **Scheduling** page (sidebar; a different page from anything similarly named under Admin) is a team-wide weekly grid: every team member's calendar and logged-activity blocks laid out side by side for the week you're viewing, not just your own.

#### Why you'd use it
Before sending a meeting invite to several teammates, use Scheduling to see who's actually free at a given time instead of guessing or asking around in chat. It's also the fastest way to see who's on **PTO** this week, and how the team's total logged/calendar time compares to its combined capacity target.

#### View, filters, and privacy
- Switch between **All**, **Calendar only**, and **Logged only** to control what counts as "busy."
- Filter down to a **Subteam** or specific people; it defaults to your own subteam(s) so you're not scrolling through the whole team by default.
- As a plain Contributor, you only see your own real name on the grid; teammates render as anonymized "Teammate 1," "Teammate 2," and so on, with their busy/free blocks still fully visible so you can find open time without seeing whose meeting is whose. Team Leaders and above see everyone's real name.

#### Free Time panel
The right-hand panel has three modes: **Common** (slots where everyone in the current filter is free at the same time), **Per User** (each person's own gaps), and **PTO** (who's out on a given day). A **Weekly Capacity** bar at the bottom shows total busy hours against total capacity for the filtered group, with an expandable per-user breakdown; same anonymization rule as the grid above.
how_to_use.notes_body:
**My Notes** (sidebar) is a running, searchable log of the notes you've attached to your own activities: the same underlying notes as the Notes tab on an individual activity, just viewed all together from one place.

#### Organizing and finding notes
Group notes by link type (Opportunity/Account/Project) or by Account, sort by date or name, and search across every note's text. Use the expand/collapse-all button in the page header to see everything at once.

#### Seeing your teammates' notes
Toggle **Show all users' notes** to widen the list to every note on activities you have team access to, grouped with an owner name under each {{crm}} record. A note is visible to your team by default; its author can mark any note **Private**, which restricts it to just them and App Admins; a private note never appears in anyone else's "all users" view, no matter who's looking.

#### Pushing a note to {{crm}}
Any note can be pushed to {{crm}} as a `ContentNote` on its linked Opportunity or Account (or, for a linked Project/Evaluation, appended as a dated update to Engineer Notes); see **Linking to {{crm}}** above for the full picture.

#### Ask My Notes
The **Ask My Notes** panel at the bottom of the page answers a question using your own notes as source material, never a teammate's, regardless of whether Show all users' notes is on. Choose **All notes** to search everything you've ever written, or **This note** to scope the answer to just the one you're viewing; either way, it cites which note(s) it drew from so you can jump straight to the source.
how_to_use.admin_body:
Admin screens are organized under **Admin** in the sidebar, in six categories. You don't need to memorize every page; just know which category to open:

- **Configuration**: Team Management, Activity Types, {{crmShort}} Field Mappings, {{crmShort}} Picklist Config, Keyword Rules, Nudge Rules, Capacity Groups, Cost Groups, Activity Templates.
- **Users & access**: User Management (roles, connections, last login), Role Management (the page-permission matrix that controls what each role can see).
- **Integrations**: Okta, {{crm}}, Microsoft Graph, Email, Slack, Sales Team Alignment, CRM Historical Import, MCP Server, and App Updates.
- **Global**: Teams, Subteams, Products, Calendars, Themes, Communications (email templates).
- **Workplace**: Flight Deck (the login onboarding checklist) and Announcements (broadcast messages).
- **Monitoring** *(App Admin only)*: App Health, Audit Log, Login History, CRM Sync, Activity Health, Nudge History, Scheduling.

**App Health** is the default screen when opening Admin; it's the first thing worth checking if something feels slow or broken. If a team-scoped screen looks empty, check the team selector at the top of the page first; almost every Admin screen is team-scoped.
how_to_use.criteriaiq_body:
ImpactIQ and CriteriaIQ connect in three parts. Set them up in this order. You need App Admin in ImpactIQ and Admin in CriteriaIQ. Neither app ever writes to the other.

### 1. Let ImpactIQ read CriteriaIQ projects

1. In CriteriaIQ, open **Admin › Integrations › n8n**. Under **API Keys**, create a key with **Access** set to **Read only**, and copy it. It is shown only once.
2. In ImpactIQ, open **Admin › Integrations** and expand **Projects (POC|POV)**. Under **CriteriaIQ connection**, enter the CriteriaIQ address, paste the key, click **Test**, then **Save**. The badge changes to **Connected**.
3. Choose how CriteriaIQ is used. Under **Primary source**, pick **CriteriaIQ** to make it the source of activities' Projects. If the CRM object is already the primary source, turn on **Use CriteriaIQ as a secondary source** instead: it adds criteria progress and a CriteriaIQ link beside the CRM's values. The primary source locks once activities link Projects.

### 2. Turn on live refresh

Without live refresh, CriteriaIQ details refresh every few minutes, and the Project details on activities overnight.

1. In ImpactIQ, the **Live refresh** section appears under the CriteriaIQ connection once it is connected. Click **Turn on**, then copy the **Endpoint URL** and the **Signing secret**. The secret is shown only once; **New secret** makes another one.
2. In CriteriaIQ, open **Admin › Integrations › Webhooks** and click **New Webhook**. Choose **Generic HTTP** and paste the endpoint URL. Open **Advanced Settings** and paste the secret into **Signing Secret**.
3. Under **Events**, tick `project.created`, `project.updated`, `project.status_changed`, `criteria.updated`, `criteria.completed`, `map.phase.status_changed`, `map.step.status_changed` and `map.task.status_changed`. Run the wizard's test, then create the webhook.
4. Back in ImpactIQ, the Live refresh section now shows **Last update from CriteriaIQ** with the time of that test. From now on, a change in CriteriaIQ shows up within seconds.

### 3. Show SE effort in CriteriaIQ (optional)

1. In ImpactIQ, a Team Leader or admin opens **My Settings › API Keys** and creates a key with only the `effort:read` scope.
2. In CriteriaIQ, open **Admin › Integrations › Overview**, open the **ImpactIQ** card, enter the ImpactIQ address, paste the key and save. Internal users then see an SE Effort card on project pages.

### If something is off

- **No Live refresh section**: the CriteriaIQ connection isn't saved yet (part 1, step 2).
- **The last update time never changes**: in CriteriaIQ, open the webhook's **View History**. A 401 means the secret doesn't match: click **New secret** in ImpactIQ and paste it into the webhook again. A 404 means live refresh is turned off in ImpactIQ.
- **Deliveries refused as too old**: ImpactIQ accepts a delivery only within 5 minutes of when it was sent, so both servers need the correct time.
how_to_use.settings_body:
**My Settings** (the gear icon next to Logout in the sidebar footer) is where you manage your own account, organized into five collapsible groups:

- **Connections**: connect or reconnect {{crm}} and Outlook. Open this first if a calendar event isn't showing up, or a {{crm}} search comes back empty.
- **Preferences**: light/dark/system Appearance, timezone, default team/subteam, language.
- **Data & Templates**: Activity Templates, your personal Non-Activity keywords, CSV backlog import.
- **Security & Access**: password, two-factor authentication (MFA), active sessions (with "sign out this device" / "sign out all others"), and personal API keys for MCP/automation access.
- **Work & Notifications**: work-week and daily hours, PTO days, notification preferences.

Use the expand/collapse-all button in the page header if you want to see everything at once.

#### Your Non-Activity keywords
Under **Data & Templates**, your personal **Non-Activity keywords** are a simple, private way to stop specific recurring meetings from ever cluttering your day list. Enter a comma-separated list of words or phrases, such as "1:1" or "Daily Standup", and any calendar event whose subject contains one of them, case-insensitively, is treated as Non-Activity automatically, exactly as if you'd clicked Non-Activity on it yourself. They apply to you alone; a teammate with the same recurring meeting on their own calendar is unaffected. In the suggestion order, they're checked after your team's own admin-configured keyword rules (so an admin rule that assigns a real Activity Type always wins) but before the AI fallback, since an explicit instruction from you should outrank a guess. Matching only looks at the meeting subject, never the body.
how_to_use.faq_body:
#### Why didn't my meeting get a suggested activity type?
Either no keyword rule matched it and your team has no configured default type (it renders a white **No Match** pill and stays fully approvable, you just pick the type yourself), or Azure OpenAI simply wasn't confident enough to suggest one. A blank guess is deliberately never invented for you.

#### What does "Non-Activity" mean, and is it the same as deleting?
No. Marking something Non-Activity just hides it from your day list; it never creates or deletes an activity record, and it's fully reversible by opening the calendar event's details and clicking **Mark as Activity**.

#### Why can't I edit this activity anymore?
Activities are freely editable for 90 days after they were created, then become read-only for you. An App Admin can still edit an activity at any time, regardless of its age. This protects the integrity of historical reporting data your Team Leader relies on.

#### Why does my activity say "{{crmShort}} link broken"?
The {{crm}} record it linked to (Opportunity, Account, Contact, or Project) was deleted on the {{crm}} side after you logged the activity. This is detected automatically (nothing you did wrong) and is just a signal to re-link it if needed.

#### My {{crm}}/Outlook search comes back empty. What's wrong?
Check My Settings → Connections first. If {{crm}} or Outlook shows as not connected (or the connection has gone stale), reconnect it there.

#### I dismissed a nudge but it came back. Is that a bug?
Not necessarily. **Mark read** and the toast/card checkmark only silence a nudge for today; if the underlying condition (e.g. no activity logged) is still true tomorrow, it reappears. Use **Snooze** for a longer pause, or **Close out** from the bell for good.

#### Who can see my draft activities?
Nobody but you. Only submitted activities are visible to teammates or Team Leaders, and leader dashboards never include draft data at all.
